attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The branch still lacks a direct non-natural lower bound for H_N^{SAT} or a nonrelativizing theorem extracting a label-free sketch from every small H_N circuit.
steps: Fix L=(log N)^d with d>1 and define A_N so that H_N^ell=A_N ell is the XOR of N^{q+o(1)} generated length-L labels per source input.
Assume SAT_L has circuits of size L^c. Substitute the circuit into each query and add the generator cost to get C(H_N^{SAT})<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.

If max{rho,q}<1+epsilon and a genuine source lower bound C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon} is available, the substitution contradicts SAT_L in SIZE(L^c) for that fixed c; since c was arbitrary, this is the valid beta=0 bridge to SAT notin P/poly.

Audit the source proof. If rows of A_N have a basis-coordinate decoder of size D_N and rank r_N with D_N+O(r_N)<N^{1+epsilon}, hardwire the r_N SAT basis parities and compute H_N^{SAT} below threshold; this is a concrete falsifier.

If r_N is much larger than s_N log(s_N+N), random label vectors produce high-complexity source functions with probability at least 1-2^{O(s_N log(s_N+N))-r_N}. Thus the semantic property C(A_N ell)>s_N is large in label space.

Any certificate Q_N contained in this property, decidable from the label truth table in poly(2^L), accepting SAT, and rejecting every label function with SIZE(L^c) circuits is a natural-proof-style object against SIZE(L^c). The route must then state a non-natural escape or remain only outside the known barrier conditionally.
Finally, rank-only hypotheses are relativizing-invalid: setting all labels to zero preserves A_N and its rank but makes H_N constant.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This cycle proves route-level gates and falsifiers only. It does not prove P != NP, does not prove C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon}, and the naturalness warning is conditional on constructivity, largeness, usefulness, and standard pseudorandomness assumptions.

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform Boolean SIZE, and all source lower bounds are measured as C(H_N)>s_N with s_N=N^{1+epsilon}.
The generator G_N is uniform or has its advice charged inside N^{rho+o(1)}; otherwise nonuniform leakage invalidates the transfer.
For every fixed target exponent c, a hypothesized SAT circuit of size L^c may be substituted independently into all generated queries.
The rank r_N is rank over F_2 of A_N; constructive low rank additionally means a row-coordinate decoder of size D_N computes coefficients of each source row in a fixed basis.

The naturalness conclusion is conditional on a certificate being decidable from the length-|U_N| label truth table in poly(2^L) time, large under uniform random labels, and useful against all SIZE(L^c) label functions.
definitions: source object: H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N-bit source inputs, where G_N is a label-free generator outputting SAT instances of length L=(log N)^d and M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}.
target object: SAT_L as the length-L satisfiability language against nonuniform circuits SIZE(L^c), with the target consequence SAT notin P/poly when the implication holds for every fixed c.

controlled interface: the F_2 incidence map A_N from label vectors ell on the generated formula universe U_N to source truth tables H_N^ell, together with generator overhead N^{rho+o(1)} and query budget N^{q+o(1)}.

target-preserving condition: beta=0 via L=(log N)^d, d>1, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, no SAT-label advice inside G_N, and the claimed lower bound is for the actual SAT label vector rather than for random labels.

steps: Define P_{r,h} as the union over all seeds of h-point SAT agreement cylinders; TT(SAT_m) is accepted if at least one valid seed is promised.
For r=O(log N), enumeration plus brute-force SAT labels gives poly(N)-constructivity; largeness at level N^{-A} forces h-r=O(m).
For every accepted seed e, build a DNF g_e that outputs 1 on positive labelled points and 0 elsewhere; it matches all h labels and has size O(hm).
If h<=s/(Cm), TT(g_e) lies in P_{r,h} and in SIZE_m(s), contradicting usefulness; with s=m^k and r=O(m), k>2 has no valid natural-useful regime.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current construction gives a sparse, generated, advice-free, non-natural anti-ball proof against unrestricted circuits while keeping row-bit latency constant and avoiding subthreshold indexed openings.
steps: Start with source length m and a distinct generated row family F_m of size R_m<=2^{D m+o(m)}; define H_m(r,x)=T_{m,r}(x).
Use a sound generated anti-ball proof for one row r*: if C(T_{m,r*})>2^{theta m}, then any circuit for H_m of size s yields a circuit for T_{m,r*} of size s+O(M_m) by hardwiring r*.
Convert the row lower bound into a multiplexed lower bound on M_m=(1+D+o(1))m bits, giving exponent theta/(1+D)-o(1).
Pad across computably kappa-dense source lengths; circuit lower-bound exponent becomes any delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
Check uniformity: deciding L_G on input (r,x) requires only canonical unranking and row-bit generation. If row-bit latency is 2^{O(m)}, then L_G is in E because n=Theta(m).

Run the negative tactic: if the proof, locator, or binding mechanism supplies an indexed row decoder with exponent lambda<theta, then the certified row has circuits below the claimed MCSP threshold, so the source proposal is invalid.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is conditional and route-level. It validates the carrier-to-E transfer and names falsifiers, but it does not construct the generated anti-ball source and does not imply P != NP without an additional NP-preserving bridge.

assumptions: Circuit model: unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits over a fixed finite basis; all lower bounds are against this model unless explicitly restricted.
Uniformity regime: G_m, the unranking map, and the padding map are generated by fixed Turing machines with no length advice or hard-row advice.
Density regime: every target input length n is within a multiplicative kappa+o(1) padding window of some source parameter M_m.
Soundness regime: the generated proof pi_{m,r*} implies the semantic anti-ball claim C(T_{m,r*})>2^{theta m}; syntactic proof acceptance alone is not enough.
Entropy regime: duplicate certificates are quotiented before R_m is counted; D measures distinct image entropy, not raw certificate count.

Latency regime: computing H_m(r,x) may scan a sequential generator for 2^{gamma_bit m+o(m)} steps with gamma_bit=O(1), while any separate indexed row decoder of exponent lambda<theta contradicts source soundness.
definitions: source object: for each source length m, an advice-free deterministic generator G_m canonically emits a distinct row family F_m={T_{m,r}: r<R_m} of N=2^m bit truth tables and at least one generated nonblackbox proof pi_{m,r*} certifying C(T_{m,r*})>2^{theta m}.
target object: the multiplexed language L_G has finite table H_m(r,x)=T_{m,r}(x) on M_m=m+ceil(log_2 R_m) input bits, padded across kappa-dense source lengths to an all-length E language.

controlled interface: the only allowed transfer operations are E-uniform distinct-row unranking, sequential or streamed row-bit generation with constant exponential latency, and certificate generation without advice; no nonuniform hard-row selector is used.

target-preserving condition: theta>0, D=limsup_m log_2 R_m/m is constant, source lengths are computably kappa-dense, row-bit latency is 2^{O(m)}, proof-generation rate is constant when proofs are used as searchable evidence, and the proof is sound for unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits.
C(f) denotes minimum fan-in-two nonuniform Boolean circuit size for the finite truth table f, up to polynomially irrelevant encoding overhead.
A row decoder is an indexed algorithm or circuit that on input (r,x) outputs T_{m,r}(x) without sequentially regenerating the full row family.

definitions: source object: the conditional generated MCSP anti-ball carrier from the previous lemma.
target object: an E language L_G with nonuniform circuit lower bounds on padded lengths.
controlled interface: the bridge uses truth-table multiplexing and padding, not NP-completeness or Karp reductions.
non-claim boundary: no membership of L_G in NP and no lower bound for SAT follows from the carrier alone.

equations.label: route_level_consequence
equations.latex: L_G\in E\ \wedge\ C_{L_G}(n)>2^{\delta n}\not\Rightarrow P\ne NP\text{ without an NP-preserving bridge}
equations.valid_when: Valid when the carrier construction only defines an E language and supplies no NP-complete source reduction.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Promotion toward P versus NP would require a separate valid NP-preserving reduction or a target language already known to be NP-complete.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This protects the branch from overstating the conditional carrier transfer as the main conjecture.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The generated anti-ball bridge yields at most an explicit E-language circuit lower bound unless an additional NP-preserving reduction is supplied; it is route-level progress and not a P != NP proof.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every plausible generated anti-ball proof requires either nonuniform row selection, natural-size projection, or lambda_open<theta indexed openings.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named proof system supplies advice-free generated anti-ball proofs with lambda_open>=theta, constant row-bit latency, kappa-dense lengths, and bounded distinct-image entropy.
control_decision.reason: The bridge is now quantitatively valid conditional on the source, and the next possible contribution is a finite no-go or validation theorem for a named proof-system binding interface.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier now requires sound generated anti-ball row evidence, not merely an MCSP-hard truth table or aggregate hardness statement.
Multiplexing and kappa padding give delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)); constant row-bit latency preserves E membership.
Explicitness splits into row-bit latency, proof-generation rate, canonical unranking, and absence of nonuniform hard-row selection.
Any proof binding or commitment must be checked for subthreshold indexed row openings.
Dense locatable projections remain quarantined; sparse generated projections do not by themselves trigger largeness.

falsifiers: falsifier: row-opening or commitment interface computes certified row bits with exponent lambda<theta
falsifier: proof or row generator has unbounded exponential rate, moving the target language outside E
falsifier: hard row is chosen by nonuniform advice rather than multiplexed rank bits
falsifier: proof certifies aggregate or average hardness but no row usable by the multiplexed table
falsifier: projection repair makes a poly(N)-decidable useful large property while excluding small circuits
falsifier: black-box transcript verifier queries o(2^{theta m}/m) row positions and can be fooled by sparse easy tables

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: If lambda_open<theta, the opening algorithm becomes a nonuniform circuit for the certified row and falsifies the source. If lambda_open>=theta while row-bit generation remains 2^{O(m)}, the bridge remains conditionally valid with delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
held_fixed_controls: theta, D, and kappa are fixed constants with theta>0 and D>=0.
The generator, unranking, and padding are advice-free and E-uniform.
The circuit model remains unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits.
The proof may be exponentially long but must be generated at a constant exponential rate.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The route now hinges on whether generated proof binding leaks a row decoder. A concrete latency experiment tests the exact distinction between harmless long proof generation and invalid indexed access.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, imagine a deterministic generated anti-ball MCSP certificate family AB_{theta,D}: it outputs R_m=2^{D m} rows, one sound nonblackbox proof that a row is outside every circuit ball of radius zero at size 2^{theta m}, and a binding commitment supporting row openings.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal opening-to-circuit lemma for the chosen proof system, plus a soundness proof that the generated certificate implies C(T)>2^{theta m} without advice-selected rows or natural-size projections.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: lambda_open, the exponent of the fastest indexed opening algorithm x -> T_{m,r}(x) derived from the proof or commitment.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 63 adds a latency ledger: constant total proof generation is not the decisive issue; the valid transfer needs constant E-time row-bit generation, while any separate indexed row opening below theta is an immediate MCSP-source falsifier. The extraction exponent remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)), and the unresolved work is a nonblackbox generated anti-ball source with no advice and no subthreshold openings.

negative_tactic_decision.conflict_target: claim of language hardness from a carrier that may only identify nonuniform hard rows or may encode a subthreshold row decoder.
negative_tactic_decision.contradiction_carrier_or_no_go_family: Opening-to-circuit leakage for the certified row, plus advice/uniformity failure in row selection.
escape_conditions: searchable certificate within E via constant row-bit latency
density control that avoids natural-property largeness pressure
binding mechanism whose indexed openings cost at least 2^{theta m-o(m)}
negative_tactic_decision.exact_negation_or_method_class: MCSP/MKtP generated anti-ball certificates, proof-binding openings, hard-row selectors, and truth-table ranking mechanisms.
negative_tactic_decision.next_validation_handoff: Send the latency-ledger packet to pvsnp-symbolic-complexity-auditor for exact parameter checking, then to pvsnp-impossibility-theorem-forger if a named proof-binding model yields lambda_open<theta.
negative_tactic_decision.paper_contribution_potential: Potential paper-level scoped theorem: generated MCSP anti-ball carriers either transfer with delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) under a no-opening condition or fail by an opening-to-circuit no-go.
proof_obligations: Name the truth-table family F_m, row rank r, verifier V, proof generator G, and certificate size or generation rate.
Check whether selection uses advice, ranking, or nonuniform hard-string choice.
Measure lambda_open for every row-opening, commitment, locator, or verifier binding interface.
Test easy sparse tables, low-complexity rows, and black-box low-query transcripts as falsifiers.
negative_tactic_decision.reason_for_tactic: The live risk is that the generated proof or commitment identifies a nonuniform hard row or leaks a low-exponent evaluator instead of yielding a uniform language lower bound.

branch_outputs.next_experiment: Instantiate the binding-opening audit for one named proof framework, e.g. an algebraic/PCP-style commitment to truth-table anti-ball constraints, and compute whether its row openings have exponent lambda_open below the claimed theta threshold.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.

Audit Karchmer-Wigderson and formula-depth transfers separately: determine whether a lifted SAT communication lower bound can validly certify formula-size or depth lower bounds while still failing for unrestricted SIZE(poly).

Audit approximate-junta transfers for low-influence or depth-2 targets: compute when Friedgut's J=exp(O(I/epsilon)) is below m for SIZE(m^k) subclasses, and separate genuine AC0/DNF progress from another unrestricted SIZE collapse.

Audit branching-program length-width lower bounds for SAT using the same exponent discipline: source object L*log W or time-space simulation, target class DTIME(m^k), and padding erosion under full input length.

Audit essential-variable and junta-dimension lower-bound routes: prove the compiler bound for SIZE(m^k), compute the universal ceiling m, and test padded SAT as the falsifier before considering any P-vs-NP transfer.
